B1.problem: a post-commit snapshot write failure locked the matter: a reload read STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE and the failure copy said the content was not saved
B1.fix: read recovery. readIntake treats a missing current envelope at version > 1 as recovery: it returns the newest older valid snapshot (or an empty form) at the committed version with view.recovery = { missingVersion, recoveredFromVersion }. saveIntake on a recovered version always writes (no 没有变化 shortcut), so the gap is filled. A malformed current envelope is still STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE. The post-commit and replay-without-envelope failures use committedWithoutSnapshotMessage, which says the version is recorded.
B1.whyNotSameTransaction: LocalRepository.commit only writes asset-backed blobs; carrying the intake snapshot in the same transaction needs a repository change outside the V6-13 write set
B1.ui: Intake.tsx shows an intake-recovery alert naming both versions and keeps the form and save button; the committed-version paragraph says the page content is kept and a reload can continue at that version

B2.problem: answers.disclosureDetail.evidenceRefs were not validated at save and not checked on read
B2.fix: each ref is checked with validateRefList and a failure returns SOURCE_LOCATOR_INVALID at answers.disclosureDetail.evidenceRefs[i] with no write; on read, QuestionView.evidenceChanged marks refs that no longer locate, sourceChanged includes them, and the view is stale. The UI lists the refs with a changed marker and a remove button.

B3.problem: when repository.commit failed its version check, saveIntake returned committed.error.latestVersion, the matter's aggregate version (it moves on every write, e.g. a target add), not sourceVersion; the conflict panel then pointed at a version with no snapshot and a retry on it could never land
B3.fix: a commit VERSION_CONFLICT now reloads the matter. If sourceVersion still equals the save's base, the commit is rebuilt against the fresh matter and retried, up to MAX_SAVE_ATTEMPTS = 3 commits. A failed version check writes nothing, so a rebuild never records a second event; with a request key every attempt also derives the same event id. If sourceVersion moved, the reply is VERSION_CONFLICT with latestVersion = the real sourceVersion and latest = that version's snapshot (the newest older valid snapshot of this matter when it is missing). If the bound is exhausted while sourceVersion has not moved, the reply is STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with MATTER_BUSY_MESSAGE (案件同时有其他写入，这次没有保存。请再保存一次。) and nothing is written.

decisions: A question's provenance stores { key, source, basedOnVersion, savedAt, savedBy }. It is written on every answered question whose value or source changed, and the previous record is kept when both are unchanged. An unanswered question has no provenance and no source.

The three sources are exactly material paragraph (a validated SourceRef), 材料中未找到, and 用户直接回答. A source is required for each answered question, and a SourceRef must still locate its chunk (same source, chunk, hash, page, start/end and quote) before a save can succeed.

Public history (disclosure) and maturity are never inferred. Suggestions only locate paragraphs that mention a keyword; they never set an answer. The UI's select starts on 请选择（不会自动填写） and the saved snapshot keeps null until the user chooses.

A conflict is a record over two or more fact ids from the same snapshot. States: open (no chosen side, no reason), resolved (at least one chosen side, no reason), retained (no chosen side, a required reason). Both fact statements are always echoed in the view, so both sides stay locatable.

Unchanged answers, facts, conflicts and provisions write no version; the reply says 没有变化. A request key is a true idempotency key scoped by (tenant, actor, operation, key): the record lives at intake/idempotency/{tenant}/{user}/intake.save/{key} and stores the operation and matter id. The key is claimed in one read-write transaction before any business write. A completed record with the same request hash replays the stored response; a committed record is finished or replays its committed outcome; a live pending claim makes the same request wait briefly, then fail retryably as busy; a pending claim past its 30s lease may be taken over. A different request hash under the key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT whatever the record's state. Only the claim owner may finalize or settle a commit; a stalled owner's commit can still land, and the deterministic event id prevents a duplicate.

Commit first, then the intake blobs, as V6-11 does for parse transitions. A post-commit blob failure returns STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with committedVersion and a message that says the version is recorded but its snapshot is missing (never 没有保存). A fresh read of a committed version without its snapshot is a recovery read, not an error: it shows the newest older valid snapshot (or an empty form when none exists) with a recovery notice, at the committed version, and the next save at that version always writes a new version with the complete snapshot.

Draft staleness is read through the V6-04 isInputStale over DraftInputRef, and bindings live in intake/drafts/{matterId}. bindDraftInput is the seam a later drafting ticket will call; V6-13 only reads the bindings.
Candidate facts are staged, never adopted implicitly. Only adoptCandidateIds enters the snapshot, and the adoption is recorded on the candidate set (adoptedFactId).

Re-suggesting a citation: the source select may encode the same ref either as the question's suggestion (suggest:i) or as the plain chunk (chunk:id). Both decode to the identical SourceRef, so the stored record is the same bytes either way.

05-contracts §2: every successful save response is replayable, including an unchanged save that writes no version. The record holds the request hash, the version, and (for a no-op) the baseline snapshot. The claim runs before the matter status gate, so an identical retry returns the original response after the matter moves or is archived while a different payload under a used key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A version write marks the record committed before writing its snapshot blob batch and completes it in that same batch; a failed batch leaves a committed record, so a same-key retry returns the original committed error instead of a conflict (review-04 N1).

After a VERSION_CONFLICT the panel offers two choices. 「保留我的修改」 refreshes the view (chunks, staleness, sourceVersion) but keeps the edited form, and the next save writes the user's text as a new version above the latest. 「以最新版本重新加载」 drops the edits and reloads. Neither merges the two sides automatically.

One atomic claim protocol serves both the no-op and version-writing branches: absent key -> put a pending record with claimId, requestHash, matterId, operation, requestKey, at and leaseExpiresAt; completed same hash -> replay; committed same hash -> finish or replay that commit; pending same hash -> one owner, bounded wait then busy; pending past its lease -> takeover; different hash in any state -> IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A pre-commit failure or VERSION_CONFLICT retry releases only this attempt's pending claim. The deterministic event id v6/intake/event/{matterId}/{requestKey} remains the backstop against a duplicate commit.
limitations: The ticket worktree did not mount the Intake panel: apps/web/src/v6/routes/V6App.tsx is outside the V6-13 write set. Browser evidence was produced with the temporary mount in mount-patch.md, which was reverted byte for byte. After acceptance the coordinator applied the permanent mount on the PR branch: the facts tab renders Intake, and navigation.ts reports the facts capability as available.

There is no drafting feature and no target-creation surface in V6-13. The browser drive injects one target and one draft input binding straight into IndexedDB (the same schema bindDraftInput writes) to show the stale-derived-draft state; the engine tests drive the real bindDraftInput instead.

The snapshot is not written in the same transaction as the commit: LocalRepository.commit only carries asset-backed blobs, and changing it is outside the V6-13 write set (packages/ and lib/ are forbidden). B1 is closed by read recovery instead. During recovery the form may show answers older than the committed version; the notice says so explicitly and names both versions.

Suggestion quotes use a fixed ±40-codepoint window. For short paragraphs the window covers the whole paragraph, so the suggestion and the plain chunk entry carry the same SourceRef; this is correct but makes the two options look identical in the select.

B4.problem: an unchanged (no-op) save returned before writing the idempotency record. After a no-op with key K a different payload under K was executed as a new version (I1), and an identical replay after other writes was no longer replayable (I5). The status gate also ran before the idempotency lookup, so a landed request replayed after archive returned INVALID_TRANSITION (I3).
B4.fix: a no-op save with a request key now records its response (request hash, sourceVersion, the baseline snapshot, unchanged: true) in one check-and-write transaction, so two different requests under one key cannot both record. Replay returns the stored baseline with unchanged: true and replayed: true. The idempotency lookup moved before the matter status gate: a replay succeeds after archive, while a new request on an archived matter is still INVALID_TRANSITION. A no-op still writes no version (S03-A03). Round 4 superseded the no-op-only check-and-write with the shared claim protocol (see fixRound4): that transaction serialized no-op writers but could not stop a concurrent version write from passing its own lookup and overwriting the record.

B5.problem: two concurrent saveIntake calls with the same request key, one an unchanged no-op and one a version write with a different payload, could both return success. The only idempotency lookup was a read-only transaction before the gates; the no-op recorded with its own atomic transaction, but the write path never rechecked the key and its post-commit blob batch overwrote the no-op record, so replaying the no-op afterwards returned IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
B5.fix: both branches now use one atomic claim protocol. After loading the matter and computing the request hash, and before any gate that can write, saveIntake claims the key in one read-write transaction: absent -> pending record with claimId, requestHash, matterId, operation, requestKey, at and leaseExpiresAt; completed same hash -> replay; committed same hash -> finish or replay the commit; live pending same hash -> bounded wait (500ms, poll 25ms) then STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with 同一请求正在处理中，请稍候再试。; pending past its 30s lease -> takeover; different hash in any state -> IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Only the claim owner may finalize or settle a commit; a stalled owner's commit can still land, and the deterministic event id prevents a duplicate. A no-op settles the claim as completed with unchanged: true and the baseline snapshot, writing no version and no event (S03-A03). A version write marks the claim committed with its version before the blob batch, then writes the snapshot, any adopted-candidate links and the completed record in that same blob batch. A pre-commit failure or VERSION_CONFLICT retry releases only this attempt's pending claim; after a landed commit the claim is never released. The deterministic event id v6/intake/event/{matterId}/{requestKey} stays the duplicate-commit backstop, and a duplicate-event or VERSION_CONFLICT failure first looks for that event and finishes or replays it.

lifecycle.claim: single readwrite transaction: get the key and conditionally put a pending record. A live pending claim of the same hash is never overwritten; one past its lease is.
lifecycle.replay: completed record with the same request hash returns the stored response: version snapshot for a write, baseline snapshot with unchanged: true for a no-op.
lifecycle.committed: committed record with the same hash has a real commit. If its snapshot exists the response replays; if not, the original committed error (STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with committedVersion) is returned, not a conflict (N1).
lifecycle.conflict: a different request hash is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT whatever the state of the record.
lifecycle.busy: a live pending claim of the same hash is waited on for at most 500ms, then the request fails retryably with the in-flight copy. It never becomes a second owner.
lifecycle.takeover: a pending claim past its 30s lease (judged from the attempt's injected now) may be replaced with this attempt's claim id; committed and completed records are never taken over.
lifecycle.release: only this attempt's pending claim is deleted, and only on a pre-commit failure or the VERSION_CONFLICT retry path. A landed commit, a committed record or a completed record is never deleted.
lifecycle.backstop: the deterministic event id and repository.listEvents metadata.version let a later attempt find and finish a commit whose record was lost.

N1.fix: a version write now marks a committed record before the snapshot blob batch, so a post-commit blob failure keeps a replayable committed record. A same-key retry returns the original STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with committedVersion and the committed-without-snapshot message, not VERSION_CONFLICT or a duplicate-event error (test 11).

fixRound4.residualLimitation: A takeover is safe for the normal interleavings: if the stalled owner commits after another attempt took over, the takeover attempt loses its version check and finishes that commit from its deterministic event. A narrow window remains if the takeover attempt then fails before its own commit and releases the claim while the stalled owner's commit has landed; the deterministic event still prevents a duplicate commit, but a same-key retry may see VERSION_CONFLICT rather than the original response. The shipped panel opens a new request key whenever committedVersion or a conflict is reported, so the product path does not use that window.
